scope: collection — consolidated metadata covering all parts of scogoai-enterprise-netops. Per-part metadata lives beside each tasks.jsonl and stays authoritative for part-level detail.

dataset.name: Scogo AI Sovereign Enterprise NetOps — Prompt Seeds
dataset.description: 12,510 synthetic enterprise network-operations task prompts (prompt seeds) sampled from the compositional taxonomy `scogo-enterprise-netops-v2`. Each record is a self-contained, fictional operational scenario — an incident ticket, on-call chat, CLI session, config review, change request, war room, audit, architecture review, or automation brief — carrying embedded evidence fixtures (configs, logs, telemetry, packet summaries, routing tables, topology) and a task instruction. Records are PROMPTS ONLY: there are no reference answers, no assistant messages, no tool results, and no ground-truth labels.
dataset.intended_use: Seed corpus for teacher-trajectory generation, model evaluation on enterprise NetOps reasoning, and rubric/judge development. This is stage 1 of the pipeline defined in docs/netops-data-contract.md; a schema-valid, review-accepted prompt is not a verified or trainable trajectory.
dataset.out_of_scope: Telecom / service-provider network operations (3GPP RAN, EPC, 5GC, IMS, spectrum planning, carrier OSS/BSS, carrier optical backbone) and certification-exam question generation are excluded by the taxonomy scope.
dataset.not_suitable_for: Supervised fine-tuning on its own (no targets), factual reference about real networks (every fixture is invented), and benchmarking that assumes human-verified difficulty labels.
dataset.distribution: private. Intended for a private Hugging Face dataset repository; see the `huggingface` section.
dataset.why_split_into_parts: The parts are generation cohorts, not semantic splits. Each part is one generator/reviewer configuration produced in its own window. Keeping them separate preserves provenance and lets a consumer weight or exclude a cohort. They share one schema and can be concatenated.

files.format: JSON Lines (one JSON object per line, UTF-8, LF line endings, trailing newline)

parts.review_independent_of_generator: mixed — 3,000 records reviewed independently, 500 self-reviewed by the generator
parts.assurance_note: Weakest cohort. Mixed reviewers: 3,000 records judged by qwen/qwen3.8-max, 500 self-reviewed by the generator. Adjudication never ran. The 3,000-record terminal run also logged 2,123 review_error rejections (transport failures, not quality judgements).

parts.coordinate_seeds: 20260820 — the SAME seed for all three runs
parts.assurance_note: Strongest cohort. One independent reviewer across every record, adjudication on 90 deferred candidates, 83-89% acceptance with rejections attributable to real quality reasons.

parts.coordinate_seeds: 20260820 — the same seed used by all three Part 2 runs
parts.assurance_note: Independent reviewer, but the reviewer deferred on ~41% of candidates (4,120 needs_verification) and adjudication using the same model family made the effective call. Strictest by acceptance rate (49.9%), least decisive by review signal.

prompt.description: The full task text handed to a model. Self-contained: scenario framing, embedded evidence fixtures, and the instruction.

category.description: Top-level taxonomy category. Constant `enterprise_netops` in this part.

domain.description: Networking domain, e.g. cloud_hybrid_networking, firewall_network_security. 25 values present.

subdomain.description: Specific technical topic within the domain, e.g. bgp_route_leak. 527 distinct values present.

difficulty.description: Sampled difficulty. Bounded per task_family by the taxonomy.

coordinates.description: The compositional taxonomy coordinate the prompt was generated to realize. See coordinates_fields.

taskgen_model.description: Model that authored the prompt text.

language.description: Optional in the schema; ABSENT from every record in this file.

coordinates_fields.taxonomy_id: Taxonomy that defines the axes. Constant `scogo-enterprise-netops-v2`.
coordinates_fields.category_id: Mirrors the top-level `category`. Verified equal in all 5,000 records.
coordinates_fields.task_family: What kind of work the task demands (RCA, telemetry interpretation, config review, next-best-action, change/rollback, abstention, architecture).
coordinates_fields.environment: Where the scenario sits (campus, branch, data_center, hybrid, cloud, multicloud, kubernetes, remote_access, enterprise_wireless, ot, ai_hpc, edge, lab_staging).
coordinates_fields.platform_scope: Enum: platform_neutral | single_platform | multi_platform. Constrains `platforms` cardinality to 0, 1, and 2 respectively.
coordinates_fields.platforms: Array of vendor/platform ids, unique. Empty for platform_neutral.
coordinates_fields.incident_mechanism: The underlying fault class the scenario encodes.
coordinates_fields.evidence_condition: Quality of the supplied evidence: sufficient | partial | contradictory | stale | missing_live_state. Non-`sufficient` values are deliberate — they test abstention and escalation.
coordinates_fields.evidence_bundle: Which artifact types are embedded in the prompt.
coordinates_fields.action_risk: How much action the task authorizes: read_only_investigation | advisory_plan_only | approval_gated_change | staging_or_simulation | emergency_change_decision.
coordinates_fields.presentation: Surface form / channel the prompt is written as.

schema.note: All 12,510 records across all three parts share one key order and one field set. `language` is optional in the schema and absent everywhere. Parts can be concatenated without transformation.

validation.scope: Re-run over the concatenated corpus, not inherited from the per-part files.
validation.method: Field-by-field check of every record against schemas/task-v2.schema.json (required keys, no additional properties, types, enums, ranges, platform_scope/platforms cardinality, platforms uniqueness, category_id == category, difficulty inside per-task_family bounds).
validation.note_coordinate_uniqueness: 9,903 distinct coordinate tuples across 12,510 records. 2,078 tuples are realized more than once, covering 4,685 records (37.4%). Of those repeated tuples, 1,645 span more than one part and 433 repeat inside a single part (all within Part 2). Prompt text is never duplicated — see deduplication.

in_pipeline.scope: Applied within each generation run against that run's accumulated corpus. No run deduplicated against another run or another part.

corpus_wide_check.lexical_near_duplicate_scan: 5-gram Jaccard over every within-domain pair in the full corpus (3,725,164 pairs, spanning all three parts)
corpus_wide_check.closest_pair: two Part 2 records in domain vpn_remote_access, Jaccard 0.0835
corpus_wide_check.conclusion: No lexical near-duplicates anywhere in the corpus. The highest similarity between any two prompts sharing a domain is 8.35%, far below the 80% pipeline threshold.
corpus_wide_check.caveat: The scan is lexical and restricted to within-domain pairs. No embedding-level dedup pass was run across parts. Semantic near-duplicates are unlikely given the lexical floor, but not proven absent.

cross_part_matrix.cause: Part 2's three runs and Part 3's single run all used coordinate_seed 20260820 with existing_records = 0, so they re-walked the same coordinate sequence. Part 1 used different seeds (20260821, 20260824-27) and shares no coordinate with either sibling.

same_coordinate_cross_part_similarity.finding: Parts 2 and 3 used different generator models, so records sharing a coordinate are lexically unrelated. The shared coordinate is a topical constraint, not duplicated text.

cross_part_matrix.implication: Topical redundancy is real even though text is distinct. Group by coordinate tuple before any train/test split that mixes Parts 2 and 3.

deepseek-v4-flash-0731.note: self-review — same model as the generator

quality_gate.outcomes: accept | revise | reject | needs_verification. Only `accept` records reach the dataset.
quality_gate.assurance_is_not_uniform: Review strength varies by part and is the single biggest quality axis in this corpus. Part 2 has the cleanest signal. Part 3 has an independent reviewer that deferred constantly. Part 1 is weakest, including 500 self-reviewed records. Weight or filter by part if assurance matters.

token_cost.note: Parts 2 and 3 are exact. Part 1 reports only its two terminal runs — the earlier chain runs' token counts were not preserved — so the corpus totals below are a LOWER BOUND.
token_cost.priced_cost_note: All endpoints are self-hosted or internally routed; no external per-token billing was recorded.
token_cost.compute_note: Wall-clock run duration summed across contributing runs, not billed compute. Part 1's figure covers its five contributing runs; the two aborted runs are excluded.

content.nature: Fully synthetic. Every config excerpt, log line, telemetry series, packet summary, hostname, IP, ticket id, and timestamp is a fictional scenario fixture.
content.no_live_access: Prompts must not imply live system access. Embedded evidence is supplied, not fetched.
content.pii: No personal data found across 12,510 records. Of 31,042 IPv4 mentions, 30,666 are private/documentation/reserved. The 376 globally-routable ones are well-known public infrastructure used as scenario anchors (8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4, 1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9, example.com's 93.184.216.34, Azure 168.63.129.16, GCP 35.191.0.0 and 130.211.0.0) plus documentation-adjacent 198.51.101.x addresses just outside TEST-NET-2. 73 email-like strings appear across the corpus, on RFC 2606 reserved domains (.example, .test, .invalid, .local) or generic placeholder names (j.smith@example.com); none identify a real person.
content.secrets: Not audited exhaustively. Credential-shaped strings in configs are synthetic scenario fixtures, not live secrets. Do not treat any token in the corpus as valid.
content.vendor_names: 101 real vendor and platform identifiers appear (Cisco, Juniper, Arista, Fortinet, Palo Alto, AWS, Azure, GCP, and others) as scenario context. Behaviours attributed to them are model-generated and were gated by an `invented_platform_feature` rejection reason, but have not been verified against vendor documentation.

non_ascii.note: All typographic or diagrammatic: em/en dashes, curly quotes, arrows, bullets, box-drawing in embedded CLI output, and math/unit symbols. No CJK, no emoji.

prompt_length.note: No tokenizer was applied. At ~4 chars/token the corpus is roughly 7.7M tokens.

distributions.note: Observed counts over all 12,510 records. Compare against the target weights in docs/netops-taxonomy.yaml. Per-part figures live in each part's metadata.json.

platforms.note: Counts are mentions, not records: a multi_platform record contributes two.

known_limitations: Assurance is not uniform across parts. Part 2 (4,010) has one independent reviewer plus adjudication. Part 3 (5,000) has an independent reviewer that returned needs_verification on ~41% of candidates, so adjudication made the effective call. Part 1 (3,500) is weakest: 3,000 records reviewed by qwen/qwen3.8-max, 500 self-reviewed by their own generator, and no adjudication. Filter or weight by part when assurance matters.

Two generator models cover the corpus unevenly: deepseek-v4-flash-0731 wrote 8,500 records (Parts 1 and 3) and cx/gpt-5.6-luna-max wrote 4,010 (Part 2). Parts 1 and 3 therefore share whatever stylistic and reasoning-pattern biases the deepseek model carries.

Parts 2 and 3 share coordinate_seed 20260820, so 1,645 coordinate tuples appear in both, covering 2,169 Part 2 records and 1,645 Part 3 records. Text is lexically unrelated (max cross-part same-coordinate Jaccard 0.066), but topical redundancy is structural. Group by coordinate tuple before splitting.
Across the whole corpus 2,078 coordinate tuples repeat, covering 4,685 records (37.4%). A naive random split will leak topically related items between train and test.
Temperature is uneven: 9,600 records at 0.9 and 2,910 at 0.4 (all from Part 1). The 0.4 subset is lexically narrower.

Observed axis distributions drift from taxonomy target weights, mostly because coordinate replacement on rejection reshuffles the sampler. cloud_hybrid_networking (868) and firewall_network_security (852) are over-represented; packet_protocol_foundations (117) and enterprise_realtime_networking (111) are thin. rf_interference appears in 45 records and ai_hpc in 167.
Difficulty skews harder than the taxonomy target: mean 6.09, with difficulty 1 nearly absent (38 records against a 2% target that would imply ~250).
Prompts are unlabelled. No reference answer, rubric score, or verified difficulty exists to validate the sampled `difficulty` integer against.
No train/validation/test split is defined and no split column exists. Any split is the consumer's to construct.
Quality was judged by LLM review and LLM adjudication only. No human review pass has been performed on any part.
Vendor-specific technical claims were gated by an LLM reviewer, not checked against vendor documentation. Treat platform behaviour in the fixtures as plausible, not authoritative.

usage.load_all_parts_python:
import json, glob
tasks = []
for path in sorted(glob.glob('part-*/tasks.jsonl')):
    part = int(path.split('/')[0].split('-')[1])
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for line in f:
            rec = json.loads(line)
            rec['_part'] = part          # provenance is not in the record itself
            tasks.append(rec)
usage.grouped_split_warning: Do not split randomly. Group by the coordinate tuple (domain, subdomain, task_family, environment, incident_mechanism, evidence_condition, evidence_bundle, action_risk, presentation, platform_scope, platforms) so the 2,078 repeated tuples stay on one side of the boundary.
